method: A Code 128 symbol is a start character, the data symbols, a check symbol and a stop pattern. Every symbol is eleven modules wide and holds three bars and three spaces, each one to four modules, so the page draws each symbol as black and white runs and wraps the whole barcode in ten-module quiet zones. Set B carries one printable ASCII character per symbol at the value of the character code minus 32; set C carries two digits per symbol at their two-digit value; 99 switches from B to C and 100 from C to B. The page chooses the shortest sequence with a dynamic program over the position in the text and the current set, so a switch is emitted only where it saves a symbol - four digits at either end of the text, or six or more in the middle - and it starts in whichever set costs less. The check symbol is the start value plus every data value multiplied by its one-based position, reduced modulo 103, and it is drawn before the stop pattern. Only printable ASCII from U+0020 to U+007E is accepted, up to 48 characters; FNC codes, Shift and GS1-128 application identifiers are not offered, so the page is not a GS1-128 label generator. The check symbol and the drawing are checked against the Code 128 specification, but a printed label still has to be test-scanned at the module width the label and scanner need. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
